keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Xia). The page gives the dynasty 'c. 2070 BC' to 'c. 1600 BC' with no area; 'direct Xia jurisdiction was limited to a small area controlled by the ruling clan' and 'outlying tribes were largely independent'. Two discs over central Henan (Yanshi/Luoyang and Zhengzhou) are the researcher's stand-in; before the Erlitou phases the page has only the undated capital names and the Xinzhai dates (1870-1720 BC).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The revised Erlitou dating is 1750-1500 BC and the culture was 'widely spread throughout Henan and Shanxi and later appeared in Shaanxi and Hubei' (Erlitou page); drawn as a culture (muted, dotted), not as a state boundary: the Xia page says Chinese archaeologists identify the Xia with Erlitou while many Western archaeologists call the identification unprovable. No area figure on either page.

ledger.note: c. 2070 BC: the Xia begins, traditionally under Yu the Great. Infobox 'Established: c. 2070 BC'; the Xia-Shang-Zhou Chronology Project 'proposed that the Xia existed between 2070 and 1600 BC' (other chronologies: Liu Xin 2205-1766, Bamboo Annals 1989-1558). Yu is 'the likely legendary figure'; the land is the researcher's reading of the page's Henan-Shanxi.

ledger.note: c. 1750 BC: the Erlitou culture spreads over Henan and Shanxi. The page gives the culture 1750-1500 BC (radiocarbon since 2007) and its extent 'throughout Henan and Shanxi', but dates no stage of the spread, so the year is the start of the revised range, a bridge.

region.text: the Erlitou culture 'widely spread throughout Henan and Shanxi and later appeared in Shaanxi and Hubei'

ledger.note: c. 1600 BC: Tang overthrows Jie and the Shang succeed the Xia. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1600 BC', 'Successor: Shang dynasty'; Jie 'was overthrown by Tang, who inaugurated the new Shang dynasty' (no date for the overthrow; the Chronology Project links it to the walled cities at Yanshi and Zhengzhou c. 1600 BC). Reviewer (ea-01-x, 2026-10-19): confidence 2, not 3: the year is the page's traditional 'c. 1600 BC', but the Henan and Shanxi extent of the region is the Erlitou culture page's reading, not the Xia page's.

wars.name: Overthrow of Jie by Tang
wars.outcome: Jie, the last Xia ruler, 'was overthrown by Tang, who inaugurated the new Shang dynasty'; the page gives no date, battle or territorial detail (the Battle of Mingtiao is not mentioned on the page; the shang-dynasty dossier names it).
wars.note: Listed with empty zones: the page names no land fought over.

certainty.note: No Xia boundary exists in the pages; the Erlitou distribution is archaeological. Soft throughout, and the polity's historicity is itself disputed.

notes: Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Xia dynasty, Erlitou culture. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). TYPE: culture, as the group scope asks ('Cliopatria lacks the Xia as a culture'); the schema describes the type as pre-3400 BCE, so a gap-filler may prefer dynasty. HISTORICITY: the Xia page says the dynasty is 'absent from the earliest Chinese texts and from Late Shang oracle bones' and that 'Western archaeologists consider the identification unprovable'; the map should draw it as cultural, not political. DATES: three chronologies on the page (2205-1766; 1989-1558; 2070-1600); 2070-1600 (Chronology Project) is the infobox pair and is used. The -1750 keyframe uses the revised Erlitou range 1750-1500 (the page's 'earlier estimates' 1900-1500); Erlitou lasted to 1500 BC, past the 1600 end of the dynasty (the Erligang overlap in Phase IV, 'no evidence of destruction by fire or war'): the shang-dynasty dossier's 1600 shape, not this one, owns Erlitou after 1600. THE SPHERE (all of Henan and Shanxi) is the page's own 'widely spread throughout Henan and Shanxi', generous against the 'small area controlled by the ruling clan' of the Xia page: the first keyframe is the narrow reading, the second the wide. A gap-filler may choose. No rulers (Yu to Jie are undated). Capital: only Erlitou as Zhenxun (archaeologists' tendency). AREA: no figure on either page.
